paper_title: VectraYX-Vision-1B: A Sub-2B Spanish/LATAM Cybersecurity Vision-Language Model with Structured Visual Reasoning and Native Tool Use

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: We present VectraYX-Vision-1B, a sub-2B vision-language model (VLM) for Spanish/LATAM cybersecurity imagery, coupling a frozen SigLIP-so400m encoder to a 1.04B Spanish/LATAM security decoder via an MLP. To our knowledge, it is the first sub-2B VLM specialized for cyber UI (IDA, Ghidra, Wireshark, Nmap, Metasploit, Volatility) that answers in Spanish, emits structured reasoning via native <|think|> tokens, invokes tools via Model Context Protocol (<|tool_call|>), and exports to llama.cpp's LLaVA mmproj format for air-gapped deployment. We report a negative preliminary visual-grounding result: despite fully functional pipelines, the current vision SFT (400-1900 steps, ~16M tokens) yields near-zero B6 scores (0.08 tool-identification), ignoring image content. We specify remediation (longer SFT, >=60% replay, lower LR) and expose a checkpoint-loader bug (unstripped llm. prefix) masquerading as training collapse. Crucially, we introduce a 3-variant ablation matrix (V0: NoPE-every-4, V1: all-RoPE, V2: NoPE+learned 2D) to study if periodic no-positional-encoding (NoPE) layers help or hurt attention over the 729-token visual block. Code, configs, and weights are released to establish priority on this architectural question. We provide B1-B5 for the text backbone, text controls, preliminary B6/B7 scores, wall times, GGUF efficiency on CPU, and a corpus of 14,596 QA pairs across 10 domains. We open-source all models and trajectories: jsantillana/vectrayx-1b, jsantillana/vectrayx-vision-1b, and jsantillana/vectrayx-vision-1b-checks.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: for (VLM) Spanish/Latin-American We build VectraYX-Vision-1B, sub-2B visionlanguage model cybersecurity imagery, coupling frozen SigLIP-so400m visual encoder to 1.04B-parameter Spanish/LATAM security decoder through two-layer MLP projector, and we report negative preliminary visual-grounding result that raises publishable architectural question. To our knowledge, VectraYX-Vision-1B is the first sub-2B VLM specialized for cybersecurity imagerydisassembly and decompiler panes (IDA, Ghidra), packet captures (Wireshark), scanner and post-exploitation terminals (Nmap, Metasploit), and memory-forensics dumps (Volatility)that (i) answers in Spanish, (ii) emits structured visual reasoning via native <think> tokens before its answer, (iii) invokes external tools through the Model Context Protocol using native <tool_call> tokens, and (iv) exports cleanly to llama.cpps LLaVA mmproj format for fully on-premise, air-gapped deployment. The system extends the three-phase language curriculum of the VectraYX line with fourth, vision phase split into alignment (projector-only), instruct (projector + backbone with text replay), and think+tools sub-stages. All four training phases have run to completion and the multimodal inference pipeline is functional endto-end; however, the current vision SFT volume (4001,900 steps, 16 tokens) yields only near-zero B6 visual-grounding scores (best tool-identification 0.08 on 50 held-out screenshots)the model generates fluent Spanish but ignores image content. We report this as negative result with the remediation specified (a longer SFT run at 60% replay and lower LLM learning rate), not as placeholder. We also identify, during construction, checkpoint-loader bug (unstripped llm. prefix) that masqueraded as training collapsea diagnostic applicable to any LLaVA-style export pipeline. The publishable question this system makes ablatable is whether the backbones periodic no-positional-encoding (NoPE) layers present in no previously released VLMhelp or hurt attention over the injected 729-token visual block. The backbone alternates RoPE (three of every four layers) with NoPE (every fourth); on RoPE layers the flattened patch grid receives spurious 1D order, while on NoPE layers the visual block is permutation-equivariant. We specify three-variant ablation (V0 released NoPE-every-4, V1 all-RoPE, V2 NoPE+learned 2D positional embedding) whose sign of B6(𝑉 0) B6(𝑉 1) discriminates the two competing hypotheses H1 (NoPE beneficial) and H2 (NoPE harmful, learned 2D helps). The author is DevOps engineer at Globant. Institutional affiliation approval is pending. This is preprint; all training phases have run to completion. Preliminary B6/B7 results are reported as negative finding (visual grounding is insufficient at the current step volume). The NoPEvision ablation design (V0/V1/V2), checkpoints, and runner are released with this preprint; their results and the remediated SFT run remain pending. The ablation design, the backbone checkpoints, and the runner are released with this preprint to establish priority on the method, not just the question. We report measured B1B5 for the phase-3 backbone, text-only backbone control confirming the benchmark is not answerable from text alone, measured B6/B7 preliminary scores, training wall times, and GGUF efficiency on commodity CPU-only hardware, alongside the architecture, curriculum, corpus (14,596 domain-balanced multimodal QA pairs across ten cybersecurity domains, dual English/Spanish tracks), benchmark design, and exact ablation matrix. We release code (model, trainer, benchmarks), configs, the benchmark suite, and all training checkpoints: inference-ready GGUF exports of the backbone (jsantillana/vectrayx-1b) and the multimodal stack (jsantillana/vectrayx-vision-1b), plus the full per-step checkpoint trajectory for auditability (jsantillana/vectrayx-vision-1b-checks). All numbers are single-run owing to compute cost; we label them as such and compensate with per-checkpoint trajectories and per-item bootstrap intervals.

sections.title: Keywords
sections.content: Visionlanguage models, Cybersecurity, Spanish NLP, Visual reasoning, Tool use, Model Context Protocol, Edge inference, Reverse engineering

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.content: Security analysts work through images. reverse engineer reads disassembly pane in IDA; SOC analyst triages Splunk search or Wireshark capture; forensic examiner scans Volatility process listing; penetration tester interprets Nmap output and Metasploit sessions. Yet the dominant tools for machine assistance in these workflows are text-only large language models (LLMs), which cannot see the screen the analyst is looking at, and general vision language models (VLMs) such as LLaVA [22], InternVL [7], and Qwen-VL [5], which are neither specialized for security imagery nor deployable in the air-gapped, data-sovereign environments where much security work happens. Two further gaps compound the problem in Latin America: (i) these models answer poorly in Spanish on technical content, and (ii) their 7B70B footprints preclude local, offline inference on the commodity hardware available to under-resourced security teams. that This paper presents VectraYX-Vision-1B, visionlanguage model targets exactly this niche: 1.04B-parameter the Spanish/LATAM cybersecurity decoder mid-tier of the VectraYX family [24]) augmented with frozen SigLIP-so400m [30] encoder and an MLP projector, trained to (VectraYX-1B, reason over security screenshots and invoke tools, and exportable to llama.cpp [10] for on-premise use.

sections.title: 1.1 Threat model and deployment setting
sections.content: We assume defensive or authorized-offensive analyst operating inside an organizations security perimeter, frequently on air-gapped or egress-restricted hosts (malware-analysis sandboxes, classified forensics workstations, incident-response war rooms). Sending screenshots of potentially sensitive artifactscustomer data in packet capture, malware strings, internal network topology from scanto third-party cloud VLM is often prohibited by policy or law. The model must therefore run entirely locally. Two adversarial concerns follow directly. First, the input images are attackercontrolled: malware sample rendered in disassembler, or crafted screenshot, can carry adversarial visual content, so we treat visual prompt injection [11] as in-scope for the safety discussion (Section 9). Second, the models tool-invocation capability is dual-use surface: native <tool_call> emission that drives an MCP [3] server can execute real actions, so tool grounding and guardrails are first-class design concern rather than an afterthought.

sections.title: 1.2 Contributions
sections.content: We make the following contributions. All training phases have run to completion; the system, corpus, benchmarks, and ablation design are complete and released. The preliminary vision result is negative (B6 near zero), which we report plainly with the remediation specified; the publishable question this system makes ablatablethe NoPEvision interactionis released with the method, not deferred. (1) negative preliminary result and an ablatable architectural question. We build sub-2B cybersecurity VLM and find that the current vision SFT volume (16 tokens, 400 1,900 steps) does not produce visual grounding: best B6 toolidentification is 0.08 on 50 held-out screenshots, with text-only backbone control confirming the benchmark is not answerable from text alone (7). The publishable question the system makes ablatable is whether the backbones periodic NoPE [16] layers help or hurt attention over the injected 729-token visual block combination present in no previously released VLM, because NoPE backbones and visual-token injection have not co-existed in released model. We release three-variant ablation design (V0/V1/V2), the backbone checkpoints, and the runner (Sections 8, 6.6) to establish priority on the method, not just the question. (2) The first sub-2B cybersecurity VLM with native visual reasoning and tool use, as deliverable system. VectraYXVision-1B couples SigLIP-so400m to 1.04B Spanish/LATAM security decoder and, unlike prior domain VLMs, emits structured reasoning (<think>. . . </think>) over the image before answering, and native <tool_call> tokens for MCP tool invocation. The complete artifactmodel.gguf plus LLaVAcompatible mmproj.ggufruns offline under llama.cpp (Section 3). The system is delivered and its efficiency is measured, even though its visual-grounding quality is not yet established. (3) four-phase curriculum extending the VectraYX line to vision. We add vision phase (4a alignment, 4b instruct, 4c think+tools) on top of the three-phase language curriculum, Juan S. Santillana with an explicit token budget, replay ratios that preserve Spanish and tool competence, and justified freeze/unfreeze schedule for 2A100-40GB (Section 4). post-hoc ablation identifying tok_emb freezing as the cause of v3B tool-use degradation is reported (7). (4) domain-balanced multimodal cybersecurity corpus and its construction method. 14,596 QA pairs over ten domains (reverse engineering, assembly, architecture, debugging, forensics, SOC, offense, crypto, competitive programming, LATAMspecific), generated from real source material and rendered as synthetic IDA/Ghidra/terminal images plus real tool screenshots, on dual English/Spanish pipeline (Section 5). (5) Two new security-VLM benchmarks. B6_vision (tool identification and answer correctness over held-out screenshots) and B7_think (thinking-chain presence and quality), both released and reproducible end-to-end via synthetic image renderer (Sections 6, 6.6). We are deliberately conservative about claims. This preprint reports negative preliminary vision result and released, falsifiable architectural hypothesis with the method to test it; it does not claim working visual model. Where results require run not yet completed, we specify the remediation and release the design rather than defer the question (Section 9).

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: General-purpose VLMs. The modern open VLM recipea pretrained vision encoder, lightweight projector, and an LLM decoder, trained in an alignment-then-instruct sequencewas crystallized by LLaVA [21, 22] and BLIP-2 [20], and scaled by InternVL [7], QwenVL / Qwen2-VL [5, 27], and IDEFICS [18]. VectraYX-Vision-1B follows the LLaVA-style projector recipe but differs in three ways relevant to reviewers: (i) its LLM backbone is trained from scratch for narrow domain and language rather than being general 7B+ model; (ii) the backbone uses periodic NoPE layers, which no prior released VLM has, raising the visual-attention question we study; and (iii) it emits native reasoning and tool-call tokens rather than relying on prompt-format conventions. Visual encoders. We use SigLIP [30], whose sigmoid contrastive objective outperforms CLIP [23] at matched compute and has become the default encoder in recent strong VLMs. Both are ViTs [8]. Our so400m/patch14/384 configuration yields 729 patch tokens with no CLS token, which we inject directly into the decoder sequence. Visual chain-of-thought. Textual chain-of-thought [28] has visual analogue: Visual CoT [25] shows that eliciting intermediate reasoning grounded in image regions improves multimodal QA. Our <think> mechanism is in this spirit but is native, trained capability (the tokens are in the vocabulary and the model is finetuned on think traces in phase 4c) rather than prompting strategy, and it is specialized to security artifacts (addresses, opcodes, packet fields, IOCs) rather than natural scenes. Domain-specialized VLMs. The closest analogue outside security is medical imaging, where MedVersa [31] and related generalist medical models show that domain specialization of the VLM stack VectraYX-Vision-1B yields large gains over zero-shot general VLMs on in-domain imagery. We argue security tooling imagery is at least as specialized synthetic-looking, text-dense, and semantically dependent on exact tokens (a hex address, CVE id, an opcode)and thus strong candidate for the same treatment. To our knowledge no prior VLM targets security-tool screenshots. Text-dense and GUI imagery. Security-tool screenshots are closer to documents and graphical user interfaces than to natural scenes. Donut [17] and Pix2Struct [19] established pixel-only reading of text-dense documents and rendered UIs; ScreenAI [4], CogAgent [14], and Ferret-UI [29] specialize VLMs for screenshot and GUI understanding, grounding, and agentic interaction. This literature supports two of our design choicesretaining the full high-resolution patch grid (text-dense frames punish token pooling) and scoring on exact on-screen tokensbut none of these models targets security semantics (what an opcode sequence does, whether decompiled function is vulnerable), answers in Spanish, or fits sub-2B offline envelope; and none emits native structured-reasoning or tool-call tokens. Text-only cybersecurity models and benchmarks. SecureBERT [2] and VulBERTa [12] adapt encoder LMs to security text and source code; CyberSecEval [6] benchmarks the secure-coding and offensive-capability behavior of generative LLMs. These are text-only and English-centric. VectraYX-Vision-1B is complementary: it is multimodal, Spanish/LATAM-first, and its text side descends from VectraYX-Nano [24], whose curriculum, tokenizer, and B1B5 benchmark suite we extend here. Compute-optimality and small models. Chinchilla [13] scaling motivates over-training small models on more tokens rather than growing parameters, which underlies the VectraYX design choice of 1B backbone trained on tens of billions of tokens for edge deployment; Phi-3 [1] is prominent demonstration that small, datacurated models can be competitive. VectraYX-Vision-1B inherits this philosophy and adds the multimodal dimension while staying sub-2B for offline inference. Positional encoding. NoPE [16] shows decoder-only transformers can learn position implicitly and generalize in length without explicit encodings; RoPE [26] is the standard alternative. VectraYX interleaves NoPE every fourth layer with RoPE elsewhere. The interaction of NoPE with contiguous block of non-causal-order visual tokens spliced into the sequence is, to our knowledge, unstudied we make it an explicit ablation (Section 8).

sections.title: 3 Architecture
sections.content: VectraYX-Vision-1B is three-stage LLaVA-style stack: frozen visual encoder, trainable projector, and from-scratch language decoder. Figure 1 (ASCII) summarizes the data flow.

The projector maps 729 SigLIP patch tokens to the 2048-dim decoder space; the projected tokens replace the <image> placeholder slot in the token sequence and are consumed by the decoder exactly like text tokens. frozen in phase 4a and optionally unfrozen thereafter (Section 4); we default to keeping it frozen throughout because the projector plus trainable backbone already provide sufficient adaptation capacity at our data scale, and freezing halves activation memory on 2A100.

sections.title: 3.2 Projector
sections.content: The projector is two-layer MLP: Linear(11524096), GELU, Linear(40962048), followed by LayerNorm. The output LayerNorm is deliberate choice: the decoder was pretrained purely on text-token embeddings, whose per-dimension scale is set by the tied embedding matrix; normalizing the visual tokens to comparable scale prevents them from dominating or vanishing in the first attention layer, without learned per-token gate. The projector is 13.1M parameters and is the only trainable component in phase 4a.

sections.title: 3.4 Visual token injection and positional
sections.content: handling We adopt LLaVA-style substitution: the tokenizer reserves an <image> special token; at data-build time the single placeholder is expanded to 729 placeholder positions, and at forward time the projected visual tokens are scattered into those positions (in-place, constant length). The visual tokens therefore occupy ordinary contiguous sequence positions. This has direct consequence for the NoPE layers: on RoPE layers each visual token receives rotary phase according to its absolute position in the sequence, imposing left-to-right order on patch grid that is intrinsically 2D; on NoPE layers no such order is imposed and the visual block is permutation-equivariant with respect to attention. Whether this asymmetry helps (NoPE layers see the patch set without spurious 1D order) or hurts (RoPE layers give conflicting 1D order signals) is an open question we make ablatable (Section 8). We extend the precomputed RoPE tables to cover 729 + max_seq_len positions so the visual prefix does not exhaust the positional budget.

sections.title: 3.5 Native reasoning and tool tokens
sections.content: tokenizer reserves <think>/</think> (IDs 14/15), The <step>/</step> (16/17), <tool_call> (8), and the turn delimiter <end> (7). In phase 4c the model is trained on traces that, given security screenshot, open <think> block (e.g., the pane header says IDA; the prologue pushes callee-saved registers; this is context switch), then emit an answer, and where appropriate <tool_call> with JSON payload consumed by an MCP server.

sections.title: 3.6 Export for offline inference
sections.content: The stack is designed to split cleanly into the two GGUF artifacts llama.cpp expects for LLaVA: mmproj.gguf (SigLIP tower + projector) and model.gguf (the decoder). Our implementation exposes export_llm_state_dict() and export_mmproj_state_dict() with no cross-tensor tying between them, so the decoder checkpoint contains no visual weights and vice versa. The decoder already matches the Llama tensor convention (RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE, GQA, no biases) that llama.cpp supports natively; NoPE layers export as RoPE layers with the rotary application disabled per layer.

sections.title: 4 Training Curriculum
sections.content: VectraYX-Vision-1B is the vision extension of the VectraYX threephase language curriculum. We summarize the inherited language phases and then detail the new vision phase.

sections.title: 4.1 Inherited language phases (backbone)
sections.content: The 1B backbone is produced by: Phase 1 (9.2B tokens) general Spanish pretraining; Phase 2 (50B tokens) three-block curriculum BlkA factual, BlkB code+math, BlkC domain+decay; Phase 3 (6B tokens) tooling specialization with 30% tool-SFT / 25% curatedcyber / 20% reasoning / 15% Spanish-replay / 6% code-replay / 4% math-replay mixture. Phase 3 establishes the native <tool_call> Table 1: Vision-phase hyperparameters (2A100-40GB, DDP, BF16). Replay = fraction of text-only anti-forgetting data. Juan S. Santillana Phase Trainable 4a align 4b instruct 4c think proj (13M) proj+LLM (1.05B) proj+LLM (1.05B) LR 1103 2105 1105 Ep. Vis:Replay Seq 1 3 100:0 60:40 50:50 1280 1280 1280 4c replay is 25% tool + 25% text. and <think> behavior in text before any image is seen. Vision training starts from the phase-3 checkpoint.

sections.title:
4.2 Vision phase (4a/4b/4c)
Table 1 gives the hyperparameters (from vision_p4.json). The
design rationale:
sections.content: Phase 4a alignment (projector only). Only the 13.1M-parameter projector trains; SigLIP and the 1B backbone are frozen. The goal is narrow: learn mapping from SigLIPs visual space into the backbones token-embedding space, so that visual tokens are legible to decoder that has never seen them. high learning rate (103) and single epoch suffice because the projector is small and the target (embedding-space alignment) is comparatively easy regression. Freezing the backbone here prevents the still-random visual signal from corrupting the language and tool competence built in phases 13. Phase 4b instruct (projector + backbone). The projector and the full backbone train (SigLIP still frozen) on 60% vision / 40% text-replay mixture. The 40% replay (conversational + CVE Q&A + tool traces, drawn from the phase-3 language mixture) is the anti-forgetting mechanism: without it, the backbone over-fits the visual QA distribution and regresses on B4 (tool use) and B5 (conversational)the same catastrophic forgetting dynamic documented for the language phases [9, 15]. The low learning rate (2105) and three epochs reflect that we are adapting converged 1B model, not training from scratch. Phase 4c think + tools (projector + backbone). Same trainable set as 4b, on 50% vision / 25% tool-replay / 25% text-replay mixture, where the vision portion now contains <think> reasoning traces and <tool_call> completions conditioned on images. The even lower learning rate (105) and two epochs sharpen the reasoning and tool behavior without destabilizing the visual grounding from 4b.

sections.title: 4.3 Compute and memory budget
sections.content: On 2A100-40GB, full fine-tuning of the 1.05B backbone in BF16 under DDP fits comfortably with the frozen SigLIP encoder at sequence length 1280 (729 visual + text) and batch size 4. We provide self-contained LoRA path (rank-configurable, on the backbones q/k/v/o projections) for the memory-constrained single-A100 case; full fine-tuning is the default because the backbone is small enough and full FT avoids an adapter-merge step before GGUF export. Token budget for the vision phase is modest relative to the language phases: the theoretical upper bound is 14,596 QA pairs (1 + 3 + 2) effective epochs across sub-phases, on the order of 108 forward-pass VectraYX-Vision-1B Table 2: Multimodal QA corpus by domain (14,596 pairs total). Domain Pairs Domain offense (offensive) soc (blue-team) arch (architecture) forense (forensics) asm (assembly) 4,282 2,254 1,973 1,347 1,332 debugging crypto re (rev. eng.) latam icpc (comp. prog.) Total Pairs 927 516 543 120 1,302 14, tokens (sequence length 1280); in the actually-run schedule (below) the optimizer sees subset of these because replay draw is without replacement and several sub-stage continuations start mid-stream, so the measured total is lower. Concretely, on 2A100-40GB DDP with batch size 4 and sequence length 1280, phase 4a ran 228 steps (24 min, 2.3 tokens), phase 4b ran 819 steps (43 min, 8.4 tokens), and phase 4c ran 546 steps (63 min, 5.6 tokens)16 tokens total, two orders of magnitude below phase 2, consuming 2.2 hours of 2A100-40GB wall time for all three sub-stages, consistent with the alignment-then-light-instruct VLM recipe [21].

sections.title: 4.4 Loss masking
sections.content: Throughout 4a4c the loss is computed on assistant tokens only (the span from after <assistant> through <end>), identical to the VectraYX language SFT. Visual placeholder positions are always masked (label 100); the model is never asked to predict visual token.

sections.title:
5 Multimodal Corpus
5.1 Overview and statistics
sections.content: The vision corpus comprises 14,596 multimodal QA pairs across ten cybersecurity domains. Table 2 gives the per-domain counts (from the released qa/*.jsonl manifests). Each record has the schema template_hint, {messages, domain, source_file}; image_path=null marks text-only replay record. image_desc, image_path,

sections.title: 5.2 Source material and dual-track pipeline
sections.content: Corpus construction uses dual English/Spanish pipeline: raw_en/ track (English source materialkernel assembly references, exploit writeups, CTF/ICPC problems, forensics documentation) and raw_es/ track (Spanish-native security content plus machine translations of the English track). QA pairs are generated per source chunk; each pair carries the source_file for provenance. representative asm record is generated from Linux kernel entry-point (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S) and asks the model to interpret __switch_to_asm disassembly pane.

sections.title: 5.3 Image generation
sections.content: Two image sources feed the corpus. (1) Synthetic renders: security-tool panes are rendered programmatically from the QA image_desc/template_hint fieldsIDA/Ghidra disassembly and decompiler panes, terminal sessions (Nmap, Volatility, hashcat, msfconsole), and packet lists (Wireshark)using deterministic templating so that the exact on-screen tokens (addresses, opcodes, CVE ids, ports) are known ground truth. This is essential for scoring: unlike natural-image VQA, correctness here hinges on exact technical tokens. (2) Real screenshots: smaller set of real tool captures grounds the synthetic distribution. The synthetic renderer used by our benchmark (Section 6) is released so the image side is reproducible without the private screenshot set.

sections.title: 5.4 Synthetic QA generation method
sections.content: QA pairs are produced by an LLM-in-the-loop pipeline over source chunks: each chunk yields questions that require reading specific on-screen entities and an answer grounded in the source, with an image_desc that specifies what the accompanying image must show. The recorded generation cost for the factual/technical subset (arch, asm, debugging, re, icpc) was $3.74 USD for 6,077 pairs over 2,029 chunks (2.77M input / 1.52M output tokens), illustrating the low cost of the approach; the offense/soc/forense/crypto/latam subsets were generated by the same method. Caveat (marked honestly): LLM-generated QA can contain factual errors and can leak the answer into the question; we describe the validation gap and the required human audit in Section 9.

sections.title: 5.5 Domain balance and its rationale
sections.content: The corpus is intentionally offense/soc-heavy (45% combined) because those are the highest-volume real analyst workflows, but retains long tail (crypto, latam) so the benchmark can measure whether low-resource domains collapse. The latam domain (120 pairs) is small and is explicitly flagged as under-powered for perdomain claims; it exists to probe, not to certify, LATAM regional grounding. Text-only replay records (drawn from the phase-3 language mixture) are interleaved per the phase ratios of Section 4; they carry image_path=null and are used verbatim to preserve tool and conversational competence.

sections.title: 6 Evaluation Design
sections.content: We evaluate along the inherited text axes B1B5 (to verify the vision phases do not regress language and tool competence) and two new vision axes, B6_vision and B7_think. All benchmarks are released and runnable against llama.cpp/Ollama-served GGUF export.

sections.title: 6.1 Inherited text benchmarks (regression
sections.content: guard) B1B5 are the VectraYX suite [24]: B1 CVE Q&A keyword recall, B2 threat classification, B3 security command completion, B4 tool selection (the projects hard mandate: released models must reach B4 above the corpus-density floor), B5 conversational quality. We report B1B5 before and after the vision phase to quantify forgetting; the acceptance criterion is no significant regression on B4/B5 relative to the phase-3 backbone.

sections.title: 6.2 B6_vision
sections.content: B6_vision is 50 held-out image+question pairs over security-tool screenshots spanning re, asm, arch, soc, offense, forense, and crypto. Two metrics per item: tool_identification 1 if the depicted tool (accepting canonical aliases, e.g. IDA/HexRays/disassembler), else 0. This isolates visual recognition from generic domain knowledge. the response names answer_correctness 1 if the response states the key technical fact the image demonstrates (e.g. context switch for the __switch_to_asm pane, buffer overflow for the unchecked strcpy decompilation), else 0. Where the private screenshot set is unavailable, the released benchmark synthesizes each items image deterministically (PIL renders of the exact on-screen text), so B6 is reproducible end-to-end.

sections.title: 6.3 B7_think
sections.content: reuses the B6 B7_think <think>. . . </think> reasoning block before the answer. Two metrics: think_present 1 if the model actually opens <think> prompts images but for block (native structured reasoning); 0 otherwise. chain_quality normalized count of distinct on-screen references inside the think block (tool name, keywords, the key fact), saturating at four references. This rewards grounded reasoning that cites what is actually on the screen rather than generic boilerplate. For models that do not open <think> block (think_present=0)including non-native baselines such as the frontier cloud VLM, which lacks the special tokenthe metric falls back to scoring leading reasoning paragraph the model does emit, so non-zero chain_quality here measures generic grounded-recall quality and is not comparable to native-token chain of the same score; we flag this distinction wherever baseline numbers are reported. B7 deliberately does not reward long chains per se; it rewards chains that reference concrete visual evidence, following the grounding emphasis of Visual CoT [25].

sections.title: 6.4 Baselines
sections.content: The mandatory comparison set, all zero-shot on B6/B7 unless noted: Phi-4-multimodal (4.5B) [1] small, data-curated VLM; the closest baseline in footprint and the fairest efficiency comparison. 1B text-only backbone the phase-3 model with the image removed (question only). This critical ablation measures how much of B6 is answerable from text alone; high score would indict the benchmark, not praise the model. Since the papers deployment claim is about sub-2B offline inference, not about beating larger VLMs on quality, we additionally report frontier cloud VLM (GPT-4o) as an explicitly labeled capability ceilingthe quality the offline model trades away for sovereignty rather than as peer baseline.

sections.title: 6.5 Metrics reporting protocol
sections.content: Juan S. Santillana at 50 items per suite seed variance alone understates the evaluation uncertainty. We do not report any B6/B7 number that has not been produced by the released harness. B1B5 for the phase-3 backbone are reported in Section 7; B6/B7 headline numbers are pending remediated phase-4b/4c rerun (see Section 9).

sections.title: 6.6 Released artifacts and auditability
sections.content: To make every number in this paper independently reproducible, we release the weights, the evaluation harness, and the training checkpoints. Concretely: Inference-ready GGUF exports: the text-only backbone (jsantillana/vectrayx-1b) full multimodal stack (jsantillana/vectrayx-vision-1b, model.gguf + mmproj.gguf) for llama.cpp/Ollama. and the jsantillana/vectrayx-vision-1b-checks, The complete set of training checkpoints for every phase (phase-1 through phase-4b SFT, intermediate steps) is released at the per-checkpoint trajectory reported in Table 3 and Table 4 can be audited step by step, including the loader-bug diagnostic (Section 9). so The benchmark harness and synthetic image renderer (bench_vision_1b.py, render_synthetic_images.py) are released alongside the model, so B6/B7 can be reproduced end-to-end without the private screenshot set. On multi-seed reporting. The protocol above calls for 𝑁 =4 seeds with meanstd where the training run permits. In practice every phase is single-run: phase-2 alone consumes 2 weeks of dedicated 2A100-40GB on shared infrastructure, and the vision phase adds 2 per sub-stage. At this compute budget, four-seed sweep of the full curriculum is not economically feasible for single-author, institution-unaffiliated project, so we report single-seed numbers and label them as such throughout, compensating partially with percheckpoint trajectories (which expose seed-level variance across the training path) and per-item paired bootstrap confidence intervals rather than across-seed standard deviations. We treat multi-seed as desired but not delivered property, and flag it as limitation (Section 9).

sections.title: 7.1 Backbone pretraining snapshot (measured)
sections.content: Table 3 reports B1B5 measured on four intermediate phase-2 checkpointsspanning the exact BlkA/BlkB curriculum boundary each exported to GGUF (F16, 2.22 GB) and served CPU-only through VectraYX-Vision-1B Ollamai.e., over the same deployment path the papers efficiency claim rests on, which these runs validate end-to-end for the NoPE architecture. These are raw pretraining checkpoints without phase3 instruction/tool SFT, evaluated single-seed at temperature 0.7. B1B4 probe instruction-following, classification, and tool-call behaviors that the curriculum deliberately defers to phase 3, so scores at the pre-SFT floor are the expected pattern, consistent with the base-vs-SFT gap documented for the smaller VectraYX models [24]. B5 (conversational quality) is the one axis base checkpoint can meaningfully exercise; across the four checkpoints it holds 0.62 0.69 band, and we read the checkpoint-to-checkpoint movement as single-seed decoding variance rather than trendone reason the reporting protocol of Section 6 requires multi-seed means and bootstrap intervals for any headline claim.

sections.title: 7.2 Text-competence regression (B1–B5)
sections.content: Table 4 compares the phase-3 backbone against the post-vision checkpoints to quantify forgetting. Two phase-3 checkpoints are included: step 8,000 (the prior B4 high-water mark during phase-3, reached with corrected 5-bucket mix) and step 20,000 (the final checkpoint used as the vision base). The difference illustrates single-seed variance across the training trajectory; step 20K was selected as the vision base because it had the best B5 of the two checkpoints (0.650 vs 0.602)the axis most worth preserving when injecting new visual modalitywhile B3 tool-match, though lower at 0.08 vs 0.17, falls within the single-seed step-to-step band and is re-established later by unfreezing tok_emb (below). Phase 4a (LLM frozen, projector only) shows no regressionconfirming that freezing the backbone preserves language competence exactly. The v3A-p2 checkpoint (phase-4b final, tok_emb unfrozen) achieves B4=0.110 and B3 tool-match=0.17the highest B4 score across the entire training history, surpassing the phase-3 high-water mark of 0.075while B5 holds at 0.602. This result identifies tok_emb freezing as the key degradation cause in v3B: the embedding table is required for the model to emit the <tool_call> token sequence reliably, and freezing it during vision training suppresses tool-use below the phase-3 baseline. Unfreezing it restores and slightly exceeds pre-vision performance.

sections.title: 7.3 Vision benchmarks (B6, B7)
sections.content: Table 5 reports measured B6/B7 results for the valid phase-4 checkpoints alongside two baselines. All VectraYX-Vision-1B multimodal scores are near zero, confirming that the current training volume (4001,900 joint steps) is insufficient for visual grounding the model generates fluent Spanish but ignores image content. The best run, v3B (1,900 steps, LR=5e-7, tok_emb frozen), achieves B6 tool-id 0.08 and B6 answer_correctness 0.06 on 50 synthetic items the first non-trivial tool-identification signal across all evaluated checkpoints. The SFT continuation (step 400 of the 4b-sft phase, warm-started from v3B) shows lower tool-id of 0.02 at this early checkpoint, consistent with the learning rate re-warming; it is included as trajectory point, not headline. Root cause of the earlier near-zero scores. Initial phase-4b/4c checkpoints (v1/v2 runs, 200819 steps) reported emb_norm164 the value of randomly initialized embedding table, not trained backbone. The root cause was checkpoint-loader bug: when constructing the vision model for inference, the loader did not strip the llm. prefix from the checkpoint state-dict keys, so no LLM weights matched and the backbone retained its initialization. The training itself was unaffectedthe optimizer updated the correct parametersbut every metric taken from an affected checkpoint measured model with random LLM. After the fix (strip llm., verify emb_norm630 preand post-run), v3B and the SFT continuation produce valid measurements. The earlier collapse interpretationthat the backbone overfit the visual distribution during 4cwas misdiagnosis of this loader artifact, not training phenomenon. We correct the record here and in Section 9. GPT-4o achieves B6 tool-id 0.940 and B7 chain quality 0.940, establishing frontier ceiling. Because GPT-4o lacks the <think> token, its think_present is 0 and its chain_quality=0.940 is scored on the fallback leading-paragraph regime (6.3); this measures generic grounded-recall quality, not native structured reasoning, and is the loosest of the ceilingsit sets an upper bound native <think> model need not match to be considered competent. Phi4-multimodal (4.5B) scores 0.440 / 0.220it identifies roughly half the depicted tools and generates partial reasoning chains, likewise under the fallback regime. The near-zero B6_correct scores across most models suggest the correct-fact metric is harder than tool identification: it requires grounding the response in the specific technical detail visible on screen (e.g. the exact function name in decompilation, the specific log field in SIEM pane), not merely recognising the tool category. The gap between VectraYX-Vision1B (tool-id 0.08) and Phi-4-multimodal (0.440) quantifies the training deficit at current scale. This result validates the falsifiable hypothesis of Section 6: remediated run with 60% replay and lower LLM learning rate is required before meaningful headline numbers can be claimed. Text-only control. The 1B backbone, no image row in Table 5 is the mandatory control of Section 6.4: the v3A-p2 backbone (the phase-4b final of Table 4) queried with the question text only and the image removed. It scores B6 tool-id 0.02 and B6 correct 0.00. This is numerically indistinguishable from the separate 4b-sft, step 400 with-image row above (0.02 / 0.00)a different checkpoint (the SFT continuation warmstarted from v3B, described in the paragraph above), which happens to score in the same bandand well below the v3B with-image row (0.08 / 0.06). Two readings follow. First, the control is not above the with-image scores, so the benchmark is not trivially answerable from text aloneanswering correctly requires seeing the image. Second, the fact that the with-image v3B row exceeds the text-only control (0.08 vs. 0.02 tool-id) is the small but positive vision signal that remains once training volume is held constant, and it is the number longer SFT run should amplify.

sections.title: 7.5 Efficiency (measured, model-independent)
sections.content: The deployment claim rests on footprint, which we can state now for the architecture independent of the vision fine-tune: the 1B decoder exports to GGUF of 2.2 GB in F16 and 0.60.7 GB in 4-bit quantization; the mmproj.gguf (SigLIP-so400m + projector) adds 0.80.9 GB in F16. The combined artifact thus fits comfortably in <4 GB, within reach of commodity offline hardware and far below the larger VLMs >14 GB F16 footprint. On commodity CPUonly hardware (Azure Standard_D8s_v3, no GPU), the 1B decoder in F16 serves at 18.5 tokens/s with prompt-encoding rate of Table 6: Released ablation designs (V0/V1/V2 in 8.2); results pending the remediated vision run specified in Section 9. Ablation NoPEvision Hypothesis tested Do NoPE layers help/hurt visual attention? Is 4096 hidden the right capacity? Replay % (4b) Projector width Encoder frozen vs. unfrozen Does unfreezing SigLIP help at this scale? Minimum replay to avoid B4/B5 collapse Does 4c think data improve B6 correctness? Does pooling 729196 tokens hurt text-dense panes? Think traces (4c on/off) Patch pooling 150 tokens/s via llama.cpp; the combined model-+-mmproj load time is under 10 s. These figures are representative of on-premise deployment without dedicated accelerator.

sections.title: 8.1 Which ablations are necessary vs.
sections.content: nice-to-have For top-tier security-venue reviewer, we regard the following as scientifically necessary, i.e. the papers claims are unfalsifiable without them: (1) Text-only backbone baseline on B6/B7. If the question text alone yields high B6 scores, the benchmark does not measure vision and the whole contribution collapses. This is the single most important control. (2) Replay-% sweep in 4b. The tool-use mandate (B4) is central to the VectraYX line; we must show the vision phase does not silently destroy it, and identify the minimum replay that preserves it. (3) NoPEvision ablation (below), because we introduce an architectural novelty (NoPE backbone + injected visual block) and cannot claim it is benign or beneficial without measuring it. We regard projector width, encoder unfreezing, and patch pooling as nice-to-have: informative for the recipe but not load-bearing for the core claims.

sections.title:
8.2 The NoPE×vision hypothesis
The backbone applies RoPE on three of every four layers and no
positional encoding on the fourth. The 729 visual tokens are injected
sections.content: VectraYX-Vision-1B as contiguous block at ordinary sequence positions (Section 3.4). This creates tension that, to our knowledge, no released model has exhibited: On RoPE layers, each visual token is assigned rotary phase by its 1D sequence index. But the patches form 2D grid with no canonical linear order; row-major flattening imposes an arbitrary 1D order. RoPE will therefore encode spurious token 𝑖 is before token 𝑖+1 relation among patches that are spatial neighbors in 2D but distant in the flattened sequence. This could inject noise into visual self-attention. On NoPE layers, no such order is imposed: attention over the visual block is permutation-equivariant, arguably better match for an unordered patch set, at the cost of losing any 2D locality signal entirely. Hypothesis H1. The NoPE layers are beneficial for visual attention precisely because they do not impose the spurious 1D order that RoPE layers do; removing NoPE (all-RoPE backbone) will reduce B6 answer-correctness on spatially-structured panes (disassembly, packet lists) more than on text-linear panes (terminal output). Hypothesis H2 (competing). The backbone was pretrained with this exact NoPE schedule on text, so its NoPE layers are tuned for text statistics; the injected visual block may be handled worse on NoPE layers because the model never learned position-free attention over dense, locally-correlated tokens. Under H2, an allRoPE variant or variant with learned 2D positional embeddings added to the visual tokens would improve B6. Ablation design. We propose three backbone variants, each run through 4a4c identically: (V0) the released NoPE-every-4 backbone; (V1) an all-RoPE backbone (NoPE disabled); (V2) NoPE-every4 plus learned 2D positional embedding added to visual tokens before injection. Comparing V0/V1 isolates the effect of NoPE presence; comparing V0/V2 tests whether an explicit 2D signal on the visual block helps regardless of the layer schedule. The prediction that discriminates H1 from H2 is the sign of B6(𝑉 0) B6(𝑉 1) on spatially-structured panes. This is, in our view, the most publishable single finding available in this system, and it is genuinely open: we do not know the answer.

sections.title: 8.3 Why this matters beyond our model
sections.content: NoPE and its relatives are increasingly used for length generalization in text-only decoders [16]. As those decoders are turned into VLMs by the standard injection recipe, the NoPEvisual-block interaction will recur. clean measurementeven negative one informs every future VLM built on NoPE-family backbone.

sections.title: 8.4 Safety and dual-use
sections.content: Because the model both consumes attacker-controlled images and emits tool calls, two failure modes deserve evaluation that we scope as future work: visual prompt injection [11] (a crafted screenshot that induces an unintended <tool_call>), and over-triggering (emitting tool calls when the image does not warrant action). We do not claim safety here; we flag it as required evaluation (Section 9).

sections.title: 8.5 Responsible release
sections.content: The corpus is offense-heavy (45% offense+SOC), so the dual-use question deserves an explicit position rather than disclaimer. Three considerations shape our release posture. First, the capability trained is interpretive, not generative: the model reads imagery an analyst already possesses (a disassembly pane, scan result) and explains it; it is not trained to synthesize exploit code, and its source material (kernel sources, public writeups, tool documentation) is already public and indexed. Second, the marginal uplift to capable attackerwho can read disassembly and run the depicted tools unaidedis low, while the uplift to under-resourced defensive teams in data-sovereign settings, the population that cannot use cloud VLMs at all, is the entire point of the system. Third, the toolinvocation path is the genuinely sensitive surface, and it is enforceable at the runtime rather than the weights: as in the VectraYX-Nano deployment, the MCP layernot the modelexecutes calls, and we condition release of the tool-calling configuration on the visualprompt-injection and over-triggering evaluations of Section 9, with runtime-side command filtering documented in the model card. We will follow staged release: weights and benchmarks first, the tool-calling Modelfile only with the safety numbers.

sections.title: 9 Limitations
sections.content: We state limitations plainly; several are severe enough that reviewer should weigh them against the contributions. Checkpoint-loader bug in early phase-4b/4c evaluation; B6/B7 pending. All four training phases completed without divergence. However, early phase-4b/4c checkpoints (v1/v2 runs, 200819 steps) were evaluated under checkpoint-loader bug: when constructing the vision model for inference, the loader did not strip the llm. prefix from the checkpoint state-dict keys, so the LLM backbone received no trained weights and retained its random initialization (embedding norm 164 vs. 630 for an intact backbone). The training itself was correctthe optimizer updated the right parametersbut every metric taken from an affected checkpoint was measured on model with random LLM and is therefore invalid. The earlier interpretation of training collapse was misdiagnosis of this loader artifact. After the fix, two valid runs are available: v3B (step 1,900, emb_norm=630) and 4b-sft continuation (step 400). Their B6/B7 scores remain near zero (tool-id 0.08 and 0.02), confirming that the training deficitnot loader bugis the real bottleneck: visual grounding at this scale requires more SFT steps or denser annotated screenshot corpus. The preliminary B6/B7 scores we report here are therefore negative result, not placeholder. The headline numbers from the remediated run, the NoPEvision ablation (V0/V1/V2, 8.2), and full post-vision B1 B5 regression table remain pending that run; the ablation designs, checkpoints, and runner are released with this preprint. The papers contribution is the negative preliminary result, the released and falsifiable NoPEvision hypothesis with the method to test it, the system and curriculum design, the corpus and benchmark suite, and the identification of this loader artifacta subtle but consequential failure mode that would have gone undetected without the embedding-norm diagnostic. Synthetic-QA validity. The QA corpus is largely LLM-generated. Two known risks: (i) answer leakage, where the question textually implies its answer, which would inflate B6 for the wrong reason this is exactly why the text-only-backbone baseline (Section 6.4) is mandatory; (ii) factual errors in generated answers, which corrupt the ground truth. We have not yet performed human audit of random sample; 200-item expert audit with inter-annotator agreement is required before publication and is not yet done. Synthetic-image domain gap. Much of the imagery is programmatically rendered rather than real screenshots. Real IDA/Ghidra/Wireshark UIs have chrome, fonts, color themes, and layout noise our renders lack. model that excels on synthetic renders may fail on real captures; the real-screenshot evaluation subset is small and this gap is unquantified. Machine translation. The Spanish side of the corpus is partly machine-translated from English source material. Translation artifacts (calques, mistranslated technical terms) may teach subtly wrong Spanish security vocabulary. The latam domain that would most stress regional correctness has only 120 pairsfar too few for any per-domain claim. No RLHF / preference optimization. Training is supervised finetuning only. There is no preference tuning, so helpfulness, refusal calibration, and reasoning quality are whatever SFT induces. In particular the <think> chains are imitation-learned from generated traces and may be plausible-sounding but unfaithful to the models actual computation. Frozen encoder ceiling. We default to frozen SigLIP. If security imagery is sufficiently out-of-distribution for SigLIPs pretraining, frozen encoder caps achievable visual grounding regardless of projector/backbone capacity. The frozen-vs-unfrozen ablation is planned but unrun. Single-image, single-turn. The current injection path assumes one image per example and short single-turn QA. Multi-image reasoning (e.g. correlating scan and capture) and long multiturn analyst sessions are out of scope. Safety unevaluated. Visual prompt injection and tool-call overtriggering (Section 8) are named but not measured. For tool-calling model that reads attacker-controlled images, this is real gap; we would not deploy the tool-calling path without it. Single-seed evaluation. Every reported number is single-run (Section 6.6). four-seed sweep of the full curriculum is not economically feasible for single-author project on shared 2A100 infrastructure: phase 2 alone is 2 weeks of dedicated compute per run, and the vision phase adds 2 per sub-stage. We compensate with per-checkpoint trajectories (exposing seed-level variance across the training path, e.g. the B5 0.620.69 band of Table 3) and per-item paired bootstrap confidence intervals over benchmark items, but we cannot rule out that different seed would move specific metric. All released checkpoints (jsantillana/vectrayx-vision-1b-checks) make the single-run trajectory fully auditable so others can extend the evaluation. Author-affiliation and independence. Corpus generation and evaluation are by the same author; the benchmark and the model share design DNA, risking benchmark-overfitting. External replication and held-out, independently-authored evaluation set would strengthen the claims. Juan S. Santillana

sections.title: 10 Conclusion
sections.content: We described VectraYX-Vision-1B, the design of sub-2B Spanish/LATAM cybersecurity visionlanguage model that reasons over security-tool screenshots with native <think> tokens, invokes tools via native <tool_call> and MCP, and exports to llama.cpp for fully offline, air-gapped deployment. The contributions are complete system and its clean GGUF-splittable architecture; four-phase curriculum extending the VectraYX language recipe to vision with replay ratios that are meant to preserve tool and Spanish competence; domain-balanced multimodal corpus of 14,596 QA pairs over ten security domains with reproducible synthetic-image renderer; and two released benchmarks, B6_vision and B7_think, together with falsifiable hypothesis about how the backbones periodic NoPE layers interact with an injected block of visual tokens. All four training phases completed (2.2 on 2A100-40GB for the vision stage) and the multimodal inference pipeline is functional end-to-end: SigLIP encodes 384384 image in 3.3 CPU-only, the MLP projector maps 729 visual tokens into the backbones embedding space, and the combined GGUF artifact (LLM 2.2 GB F16 + mmproj 0.82 GB) runs offline under llama.cpp. The valid phase-4 checkpoints (v3B step 1,900 and 4b-sft continuation at step 400) produce near-zero B6/B7 scores, indicating that the current vision SFT volume is insufficient for visual groundingthe model generates fluent Spanish but ignores image content. longer SFT run with denser annotated screenshot corpus is the immediate next step. B6/B7 headline numbers and the NoPEvision ablation remain pending that run. The paper contributes design, corpus, evaluation methodology, and the identification of subtle checkpoint-loader bug that masqueraded as training collapsea diagnostic lesson for any LLaVA-style export pipelinemost importantly, the textonly-backbone control that would expose non-visual benchmark, and the NoPEvision ablation whose outcome we genuinely cannot predict. Impact. If validated, VectraYX-Vision-1B would be the first tool for security analysts in data-sovereign, Spanish-speaking, resourceconstrained settings that can look at the screen they are looking at, reason about it, and actwithout sending byte to the cloud. Even if the quality falls short of 7B general VLMs, the efficiency and sovereignty envelope (sub-4 GB, offline, Spanish-native, securityspecialized) is unoccupied. Future work. Beyond completing the runs and the mandatory audits: multi-image and multi-turn analyst sessions; safety evaluation of visual prompt injection and tool-call over-triggering; preference optimization for faithful reasoning chains; and extending the NoPEvision study to learned-2D-positional variant to separate the effect of NoPE from the effect of any explicit spatial signal on the visual block.
